title: Direct, indirect and total effects
summary: A predictor can affect an outcome directly and through mediators; the total effect is the sum of the direct effect and every indirect route.

body.text: The [[direct-effect]] of X on Y is the path X → Y. An [[indirect-effect]] runs through one or more mediators and equals the product of the paths along its route; each route is a [[specific-indirect-effect]]. The [[total-effect]] is the direct effect plus all indirect effects (Bollen 1987).

body.caption: PEOU affects BI directly and indirectly through PU.

body.display: total = c′ + Σ (product of the paths along each indirect route)
body.explanation: c′ is the direct path. In TAM: indirect PEOU → PU → BI = .498 × .501 = .249; total = .128 + .249 = .377.

body.text: In larger models, such as the DeLone & McLean example, a construct can reach the outcome along several routes. SEM Lab lists every specific indirect effect separately, so you can say which route carries the effect, and bootstraps each one.

mistake.title: Judging a predictor by its direct path alone
mistake.text: PEOU's direct path to BI is small (.128), but its total effect (.377) is not. Concluding that PEOU "does not matter" ignores the route through PU.

tryIt.task: Open the DeLone & McLean example and run it. In the effects table, find the specific indirect effect SYSQ → SAT → NB and the total effect of SYSQ on NB.

checks.question: X → M = .60, M → Y = .50 and X → Y = .20. What are the indirect and total effects of X on Y?

options.feedback: Indirect effects multiply along a route; they are not sums of paths.
The total effect also includes the direct path .20.
.10 is .60 − .50; effects along a route are products.

checks.explanation: Multiply along routes, add across routes.

checks.question: What is the difference between a specific indirect effect and the total indirect effect?

options.text: A specific indirect effect is one route through particular mediators; the total indirect effect sums all routes.
options.feedback: Correct. With one mediator they coincide.
They differ whenever there is more than one route, as in the DeLone & McLean model.

options.text: The specific indirect effect excludes the direct path, the total indirect effect includes it.
options.feedback: Neither includes the direct path; that is the total effect.

checks.explanation: Specific = one route; total indirect = all routes; total = direct + total indirect.
